audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim in APiCS survey 50, sect. 4 Phonology (file now saved; none was held before). (2) Deciding source is a 2013 specialist survey sketch (Colot & Ludwig), exact languoid match, categorical statement 'always on the last syllable' -> fixed final, matching rule 01 001 0001... (3) Independent confirmation fetched sources now: Bonan 2013 p. 72 ('the foot must always be iambic'); Delumeau 2006 thesis is silent on word stress. No phonology-typed work exists in Glottolog's 89 refs; the one instrumental study (Iskrova 2009 BLS) could not be fetched sources because the LSA proceedings host timed out, but as an intonation study of a French-lexifier creole it is expected to refine (word vs phrase-final prominence) rather than contradict. (4) The record's grade field is empty although the quote is now held, verified, and corroborated by a second open source; recommend

sources.quote: Word stress is always on the last syllable. Phrase and sentence stress is also in final position.

sources.quote: As a generalization, it is possible to say that in GC the foot must always be iambic (that is, an unstressed syllable followed by a stressed one) and that the weak syllable needs to have an overt onset.
